draft.title: Natural selection
card: Individuals in a population vary. Some of this variation is inherited, which means it is passed from parents to offspring in their genes.
More offspring are born than can survive. Food, water and space are limited, so many die before they can breed.
An inherited trait that helps an individual survive in its environment makes it more likely to live and breed. It then passes the trait on to more offspring.
Over many generations, the helpful trait becomes more common in the population. This process is natural selection.
draft.remember: Helpful inherited traits mean more survivors breed, so the trait spreads over generations.

a.q: Which statement best describes how natural selection changes a population?
opts: Helpful inherited traits lead to more offspring, so they spread
Helpful traits appear when individuals need them, then pass on
Helpful traits let individuals live longer and change form
Individuals that try harder to survive pass on their effort
a.why: Natural selection works on inherited variation. Those with helpful traits leave more offspring, so the trait becomes more common. It is wrong to say traits appear when needed, because the variation is already there and inherited.
a.clue: Think about who has more offspring, and what the offspring inherit.

b.q: A beetle population on a farm has green and brown beetles. Birds eat more green beetles than brown ones, and colour is inherited. What is most likely after many generations?
opts: Brown beetles will make up more of the population
Green beetles will turn brown during their lives
All beetles will be brown after one generation
Brown beetles will be born because the beetles need them
b.why: Brown beetles are eaten less, so more of them survive and breed. They pass on their colour, so brown becomes more common over generations. Individual beetles do not change colour to suit their need, and the change is gradual, not instant.
b.clue: Which beetles are more likely to survive and breed, and what do their young inherit?
